title: Integral reduction preserves bounded constructibility
statement: Use [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. For a finite-dimensional normed extension E/Qℓ, a scheme X whose topological space is noetherian, and an integral bounded constructible complex M, actual derived reduction of M modulo ℓ is bounded constructible over the residue coefficient ring.

proof.text: Install the kernel, cokernel and extension closure proofs of integral constructible modules as explicitly typed local instances. Use the proved weak Serre triangulated-closure instance, explicitly, rather than the upstream noetherian-only instance. Apply the mapping-cone reduction theorem with the supplied actual tensor description.

Restriction along the quotient coefficient epimorphism is fully faithful on module objects, by cancelling its tensor with the module in the linearity equation. Its extension-restriction counit is invertible.

Extension preserves finite presentations by transporting finite free presentations and cokernels. Restriction therefore reflects finite presentation, locally and on each stratum using coefficient-pull compatibility. Exact faithful restriction reflects boundedness and identifies homology. Apply these reflections to the restricted reduction.

lean.statement:
theorem integralReduction_boundedConstructible (X : Scheme.{u})
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X] (M : integralConstructible ℓ E X) :
    boundedConstructible
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} (integralResidue ℓ E)) X)
      ((integralReduction ℓ E X).obj M.obj)
